video_title: Building ChatGPT for Finance — Joseph Kim, OpenAI's Head of Financial Services
gist: OpenAI's Joseph Kim explains how ChatGPT for Financial Services (design partners Morgan Stanley and Evercore) was built: ~95% on public ChatGPT/Codex plugin primitives, with bundled in-house data because third-party finance MCPs showed 40%+ error rates. He predicts 2027 models move up from junior-analyst tasks toward associate/MD work (taste, investment ideas), says GDP-eval and existing financial evals are saturated or broken, and argues safety should mirror human hierarchies of review.

insights.claim: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, an enterprise product adding firm-specific templates and data sources such as S&P, developed with design partners Morgan Stanley and Evercore.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: OpenAI is moving first-party into vertical finance software, competing with finance AI startups.

insights.claim: OpenAI tested third-party financial data MCP connectors and found error rates of 40% or more on some big-name providers, leading it to bundle data such as earnings call transcripts in-house despite customers possibly paying twice for licenses.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Data providers' MCP quality is a weakness; owning the data pipeline is a moat.
insights.quote: some big names 40% plus error rate on their MCPs

insights.claim: Joseph Kim says the number one thing customers call out about ChatGPT for Financial Services is the bundled data.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Data integration, not model capability, is the key enterprise differentiator.

insights.claim: Kim's thesis was that Codex gets about 80% of the way to a successful finance product but launching Codex alone as a finance product would fail, making the remaining 20% (data, UI, integrations) pivotal.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Vertical value lies in the last-mile 20% atop horizontal agents.

insights.claim: About 95% of what OpenAI built for its finance product could have been built by a startup using the same ChatGPT plugin architecture and primitives, and Kim predicts a billion-dollar business will be built on top of a ChatGPT plugin.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: ChatGPT plugins as a distribution platform for vertical startups.
insights.quote: I really do think that there's going to be a billion-dollar business built on top of a uh ChatGPT plugin

insights.claim: OpenAI puts its financial reasoning training data into the main 'big run' model (e.g., GPT-6 Astra) rather than a separate finance model, so the capabilities are available to all API builders.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Finance capability is commoditized across all builders, not exclusive to OpenAI's product.

insights.claim: Kim's main enterprise lesson is that products must be built around industry realities such as competitive forces and incumbent objectives, since first-principles reasoning alone leads to the wrong product.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Vertical AI winners need domain-specific go-to-market judgment.

themes.theme: Codex adoption signal in non-engineering work

insights.claim: Inside OpenAI, Codex adoption among finance, legal and sales staff was near zero and then jumped to about 90% after the Codex desktop app was released in February, whereas software engineering adoption rose steadily.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Form factor (desktop app) unlocks non-technical knowledge-worker adoption.

insights.claim: OpenAI describes itself internally as a research and deployment company, deliberately ordering research first and product surface second.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Product roadmap follows model capability trajectory.

insights.claim: An OpenAI speaker in the opening clip says the company ran into pre-training problems that limited model scaling but solved many of those issues in 2026.
insights.speaker: OpenAI speaker (opening clip)
insights.so_what: Renewed pre-training scaling could accelerate capability gains into 2027.
insights.quote: In 2026, we've been able to solve many of these issues.

themes.theme: Moving up the finance value chain in 2027

insights.claim: Kim says AI in finance has so far focused on junior-analyst work like Excel models and slides because models execute concrete instructions well and humans dislike that tedious work, and predicts that in 2027 models will move up to associate and MD-level tasks.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Pressure on junior banking headcount first, then higher-level roles.

insights.claim: Kim expects models to become much better in 2027 at human taste on softer, comparative objectives such as slide aesthetics, which is what they lack today, while factual hallucinations have already greatly improved.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Remaining barrier to banker-quality output is taste, being actively trained.

insights.claim: OpenAI trains taste with pairwise human-preference reward models, e.g. humans picking the better of two slides, because humans judge aesthetics within seconds better than grading models that burn reasoning tokens and may still be wrong.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Expert human feedback remains a valuable input for finance AI.

insights.claim: Kim argues coding, roughly 80% solved, is the precedent for finance: both combine verifiable rewards (code compiles / Excel model sums, no reference errors) with taste (clean design / the 'feel' of a model when inputs are perturbed).
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Finance automation may follow coding's adoption curve.

insights.claim: Kim says generating investment theses is harder to train because objectives become fuzzy and may take three years to validate, but calls it not insurmountable given base-model scaling, expert P99.9 feedback and research focus, which his team is prioritizing.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: AI-generated investment ideas are an explicit OpenAI target for 2027.

insights.claim: Kim says a key OpenAI advantage in coding was that model trainers knew what good code looks like, an advantage it lacks in finance, so it is hiring financial subject matter experts alongside product managers for investment banking, equity research and asset management.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Demand for finance professionals in AI training roles will rise.

insights.claim: Kim says great product management is in some ways the main bottleneck to winning in finance AI.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Domain PM talent, not models, constrains vertical AI.

insights.claim: The current ChatGPT for Financial Services is designed as a human-in-the-loop productivity tool, where the analyst first attempts each task with ChatGPT, getting 30%-80% of the way depending on the task, and remains responsible for review.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Liability stays with users for now, easing enterprise adoption.

insights.claim: Kim says OpenAI plans to shape agent security like a person's, using read/write permissions akin to Google's readability and banking's analyst-associate-VP-MD review hierarchy, as agents become more autonomous through 2027-2028.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Existing bank control frameworks can absorb AI agents, speeding adoption.

insights.claim: Kim argues the fear that a single mistake ends a finance career is misplaced, because career-ending errors are factual errors that change conclusions, which models are rapidly improving on, and layered review makes it very unlikely such errors reach an MD.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Risk aversion should not block analyst adoption.

insights.claim: OpenAI no longer reports or tracks GDP eval because it is completely saturated and the unsaturated portions are essentially broken.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Public knowledge-work benchmarks no longer differentiate frontier models.

insights.claim: When GPT-6 showed little change on financial evals, OpenAI found the evals were saturated and remaining misses were due to incorrect answer keys and poorly specified prompts, so there is no good financial eval today.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Vendor finance benchmark claims should be treated skeptically.

insights.claim: Kim's team is building an investment banking eval designed to predict whether a model can automate much of a junior IB analyst's work.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: A forthcoming metric for measuring banking automation potential.

insights.claim: Kim says ChatGPT for Financial Services is enterprise-first but OpenAI is working to bring it to prosumers on the Pro plan.
insights.speaker: Joseph Kim
insights.so_what: Wider distribution threatens retail-facing finance AI tools.
